items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: I got recruited even though I was only twelve... So I was sitting up there in this sax section... Donny James and his Orchestra.

ctx.x: — in my history. My dad, who actually was a great runner, qualified for the 1928 Olympics, went to Wesleyan, but loved music. And was a pretty decent soprano saxophone player. You can relate to that, had a nice Buescher soprano saxophone which he played at Wesleyan. He graduated in 1928. But then he became a self-taught jazz piano player and was actually a very good piano player. And my earliest remembrances are dad, when he’d come home from work at night, he would play the piano. And he would play all the great…

in this sax section just, just loving it. And so then I got a clarinet because you know you have to double, and so I thought of myself as a clarinetist and saxophone player. My dad at this point began having jam sessions in our house and we’d invite people over. And my high school music teacher, a guy named Chief McNally, who was a trombonist, had been brought up and his parents were Salvation Army folks. And you’re not supposed to leave the Army. You’re supposed to stay in the Salvation Army if you’re a child.…
